gen-fs-nippo-gf-karla: Karla stands tall and stocky, its middle band swollen up. Nippo's round bowls hold a single line thickness, so a long page of paragraphs feels sturdy and easygoing.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-kedebideri: Nippo looks cut from wire, its small letters standing almost capital-sized. Next to Kedebideri's skyward x-height and rounded, inviting forms, that no-modulation line becomes the pair's sharpest quality.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-khula: Khula has a tall midsection, like a squat brush-pen belly, with curves holding their mouths open. Nippo's unvaried strokes sit above it, so a long passage of sans-serif text goes down smoothly and without fuss.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-krub: Krub carries a pronounced x-height and curves that lift away before closing the loop. Nippo, with every stroke ending at one measured thickness, earns its place in big, short headings.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-kufam: Technical and bright, Nippo's near-capital small letters look cut from wire. Nippo is best at crisp, standout display lines, while Kufam, a sans-serif with neon-tube strokes and open e curves, handles the running text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend: Wiry and upright, Nippo leads with small letters almost the height of capitals. Lexend's outsized lowercase and open curves like generous room, so nudge its size up a notch and the sans text breathes.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-deca: Nippo's lowercase stand nearly as tall as capitals, drawn like bent wire with a technical edge. And where it excels at striking display lines, Lexend Deca's plain, unshaded sans handles quiet reading with big lowercase.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-exa: Nippo sets a technical tone, with small letters standing proud and strokes that look cut from wire. Lexend Exa follows with wide-open curves and stubby ascenders, so a long stretch of sans text moves along cleanly.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-giga: Wire-cut and technical, Nippo's small letters nearly reach capital height, while Lexend Giga's sans lines lie flat and generously tracked. The pair's strongest quality is its openness.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib, its body height nearly matching capitals and every c visibly gapped. Nippo's wire-cut lettering gives it a technical, contemporary edge.
